key_insight: Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) separates knowing what a robot should do from learning how to do it. It combines pretrained visual-language understanding with simulation-based training for robot control.
problem_solved: Robot policies must connect scene and task understanding to executable movements, including when familiar concepts appear in new combinations.
method: Use a pretrained 27-billion-parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning.
Connect an off-the-shelf vision-language model to robot controls through a simple tool harness.
Apply supervised fine-tuning and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on simple simulated tasks to teach robot movement.
impact: ZAP offers practitioners a recipe for combining pretrained semantic knowledge with simulation-trained control. The approach targets compositional generalization, although the provided abstract does not quantify performance or real-world transfer.
visual_elements: Two-part diagram: pretrained understanding ('what') plus simulation-trained control ('how') leading to robot action.
Training pipeline: pretrained knowledge → supervised fine-tuning → GRPO in simulation → robot policy.
Tool-harness schematic linking a vision-language model to robot movement commands.
Illustration of familiar objects and actions recombined into a new task.
paper_title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
paper_authors: Benjamin Pikus, Daniel Saunders, Mircea Mironenco, Salman Mohammadi, Mathew Mathew
